lessons.title: Counting and recording stock
lessons.html:
What are stock levels?

A stock level is how much of an item the store has. Managers need to know stock levels to order on time, to stop theft and to know how much money is tied up in stock.

Ways to keep track

  • Stock card or bin card: a card for each item. Every time stock comes in or goes out, it is written down and the balance is worked out.
  • Computer system: the till and receiving system add and subtract stock automatically. People must still count to check it is right.

Working out the balance

Balance = opening stock + received − sold − damaged or returned to supplier.

DateInOutBalance
1 June opening60 bags
3 June delivery40100
4 June sold2575
6 June sold3045

Counting stock

  1. Get the count sheet for your area.
  2. Count each item. Count in units the system uses: bags, litres, metres, boxes.
  3. For pallets, count bags per layer and multiply by the number of layers. Check that the middle is full.
  4. Write the number clearly in pen. If you make a mistake, cross it out with one line and write the new number next to it.
  5. Do not count stock that has been sold but not yet collected. Mark it separately.
  6. Sign the count sheet.

Counts are often done with two people: one counts and one writes. This helps stop mistakes.

lessons.title: Using stock levels to make decisions
lessons.html:
Comparing count with records

After counting, compare your count with the stock card or system. The difference is called a variance.

  • Count lower than records: stock is missing. It may be theft, damage, a sale not captured, or a delivery recorded wrongly.
  • Count higher than records: maybe a delivery was not captured, or the wrong code was used at the till.

Report all variances to your supervisor. Do not change numbers to make them match.

Minimum, maximum and re-order levels

LevelMeaning
MinimumThe lowest safe amount. Below this, the store may run out.
Re-order levelWhen stock reaches this number, order more.
MaximumThe most the store should hold. More is money stuck on the shelf.

Example

Wire: re-order level 20 rolls, maximum 80 rolls. Count shows 18 rolls. Stock is below re-order level, so tell the buyer. They may order up to about 60 rolls so the store does not go over its maximum.

Seasons change the levels

In spring, maize seed and fertiliser sell fast, so the levels go up. In autumn and winter, lick and feed sell more. A good stock controller watches the season and talks to the buyer.

Slow and dead stock

Some items sit on the shelf for months. Write them on a list for your manager. They may go on special before they expire.

Key points

  • Balance = opening + in − out.
  • Count carefully, in the right units, and sign the sheet.
  • A variance is the difference between count and records; report it.
  • Order when stock reaches the re-order level.
  • Never change numbers to make them match.
